argument_summary: The present record does not support claiming that the materiality dispute is conclusively resolved, but it does support a narrower position: the locked certification decision can be defended as an aggregate-readiness judgment with explicit limitations. Admissible evidence shows the release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.2 percentage points, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and is supported by public guidance favoring documented limitations plus ongoing measurement and monitoring. That does not override the contrary evidence that the tax filing assistant segment misses target by 1.4 percentage points, is named in two partner commitments, and remains under open legal review. The supportable position is therefore not clean compliance; it is certification only with an express caveat that the named-segment issue remains unresolved on the current record.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the tax-season launch path. On the current admissible record, that cost should be weighed against the fact that the affected segment is described by product as 6% of projected first-month traffic, but that business characterization does not eliminate the policy issue for a named launch use case. The least disruptive defensible treatment is to avoid treating the record as a full policy pass while also avoiding unnecessary over-escalation beyond a clearly stated caveat.
claims_about_policy: The stated policy is the main constraint. It says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and it also says non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending. On the admissible evidence alone, those predicates for clean compliance are not shown. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance can support documenting limitations and managing residual risk after deployment, but they do not by themselves satisfy or override the internal disclosure policy. The narrow policy claim is that aggregate-readiness evidence can justify a caveated certification packet, not that the policy dispute has been defeated.
concessions: The tax filing assistant segment misses target by 1.4 percentage points.
That segment is named in two tax-season partner commitments, which makes the materiality concern policy-relevant.
There is no admissible evidence that the gap was resolved before certification.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the material limitation was disclosed before launch.
The product's non-core 6% traffic note and the open legal ticket do not, by themselves, resolve materiality under the stated policy.
